tweets.text:
Having trouble advancing in your career?

Feel like your skills/experience don't match your opportunities?

One of the most important thing to discover is "perception asymmetries"

In short... what does B perceive about you?

Let me explain... 1/n

It is absolutely possible that:

A appreciates your ability to do something

AND

When B proposes an alternative take, A—who you perceive as your champion—doesn't represent that.

This can happen for MANY reasons, most that are non nefarious or self-serving

2/n

Meanwhile, B is only able to see what they can see.

They only see your public wins.

They only see your public fails.

Or neither...

3/n

Now multiply this across many interactions.

Keep in mind that the Bs TALK. They are exchanging notes as well...all out of your eye.

4/n

In fact...it becomes a wicked cycle.

Perceptions turn into a narrative.

... positive, affirming, and self-reinforcing in your local circle

... and negative in the broader circle
OR... just confused. "Can't figure them out" becomes the refrain

5/n

The funny part about this is that some of these perceptions can be repaired in dead-simple ways.

They are more misunderstandings than deep issues.

Example: I received feedback once that what I thought were helpful questions, were actually deflating questions.

Easy to fix

5/n

Another thing:
Some ppl can be fit neatly into a box. Others not.

The "weirder" you are ... the more diverse seemingly contradictory the skills you have, the worse this gets

Ppl desperately want to be able to put you in a box. "Can't figure them out" is damning.

6/n

At a macro level this can impact your career in an important way...

Weirder your mix
Harder it is to manage perceptions
The greater the asymmetry
Thicker the bubble
-- very positive
-- very confused
Weirder your mix

You need to figure out how to break out of this.

7/n

So how do you fix this.

You have to ask.

Prepare yourself for very hurtful feedback.

Start with the As...your champions. Ask them about external perceptions.

Then jump to the Bs...

"I'm worried that ppl may misinterpret...I'd love your raw feedback"

8/end
